MappedPercent.note: samtools flagstat on each sequencing run's own alignment, before merging and filtering (MultiQC section 'LIB: SAMTools', rows <sample>_REP<n>_T<run>): the first of the release's four flagstat sections, so MultiQC 1.13 writes it as multiqc_samtools_flagstat.txt and the other three as _1 (merged library, unfiltered), _2 (filtered) and _3 (merged replicates); verified against multiqc_sources.txt on 2.1.2-local-test. mapped_passed_pct is already a percentage. A replicate sequenced once is its run _T1; one sequenced over several runs is a multi-run sample and gets no backfill.

FingerprintJSD.note: deepTools plotFingerprint's Synthetic JS Distance: the Jensen-Shannon distance between the library's fingerprint (cumulative coverage over genome bins) and a uniform, synthetic one, 0 to 1, higher meaning more enrichment. The release passes no --JSDsample, so the plain JS Distance column is never written; verified on the narrow-peak -profile test run. Read from <sample>.mLb.clN.plotFingerprint.qcmetrics.txt (each replicate's merged, filtered library). Multi-run samples get no backfill.

TSSEnrichment.note: ataqv's TSS enrichment score (metrics.tss_enrichment in <sample>.ataqv.json, each replicate's merged library): coverage at transcription start sites over flanking background, higher meaning better signal to noise. The JSON also lists every peak, so on a large run some files may exceed the harvest's caps and are then recorded as truncated and give no value. Verified on 2.1.2-local-narrow, where ataqv writes tss_enrichment as null for the single-end replicates (T100, T150), so they get none. Multi-run samples get no backfill.

DuplicationPercent.note: Picard MarkDuplicates on each replicate's merged library, before filtering: the only MarkDuplicates table in the release's MultiQC config with no anchor, so MultiQC 1.13 writes it as multiqc_picard_dups.txt (1.13 writes its tables as text whatever the config's data_format: yaml says), rows named <sample>_REP<n> after the config's extra_fn_clean_exts. The table keeps Picard's 0-1 fraction, so $derived.duplication_pct multiplies it by 100. A replicate sequenced over several runs is a multi-run sample and gets no backfill. The merged-replicate MarkDuplicates table MultiQC writes under its own anchor (mrep_picard) is not read: its rows are the replicate groups, which have no D.SEQ of their own. Table name, row names and the fraction checked against the 2.1.2 -profile test run (fixture 2.1.2-local-test)

deliberately_unmapped.why: The replicate's FRiP score, a 0-1 fraction; its peak row's FRiPPercent reads it as a percentage through $derived.frip_pct (a merged replicate's row reads mrep_frip, the group's own).
The replicate's peak count; its peak row's PeakCount reads it through $derived.peak_count (a merged replicate's row reads mrep_peak_count).
Picard's 0-1 fraction; DuplicationPercent reads it as a percentage through $derived.duplication_pct.
Picard's library name (the read group's LB), not a measurement.
A read count; D.SEQ's read counts come from the sequencing, not from one alignment step.
A read-pair count; D.SEQ's read counts come from the sequencing, not from one alignment step.
A count of secondary and supplementary records: no D.SEQ attribute means it.
A count of unmapped reads in the merged library; MappedPercent reads samtools flagstat's percentage per sequencing run instead.
A duplicate count; DuplicationPercent records the duplicate share from the same table.
A duplicate count; DuplicationPercent records the duplicate share from the same table.
Optical duplicates, a subset of the duplicates DuplicationPercent counts: no D.SEQ attribute means it.
Picard's estimate of unique molecules in the library: a library-complexity measure no D.SEQ attribute means.

unmapped_files.why: FastQC reports on the raw reads; QC, not a result of the analysis.
Trim Galore logs, FastQC of the trimmed reads, and the trimmed reads themselves (with --save_trimmed): an intermediate of the registered alignment.
Library-level alignments (with --save_align_intermeds), their samtools stats, STAR logs and unmapped reads (with --save_unaligned): intermediates of the merged-library BAM the aln rule registers.
Merged, duplicate-marked and pre-orphan-removal BAMs (with --save_align_intermeds): earlier states of the filtered clN BAM the aln rule registers.
The orphan-removed alignment before sorting (with --save_align_intermeds): the same reads as the sorted clN BAM the aln rule registers.
samtools, Picard and Preseq QC of the merged alignments; summarised in the MultiQC report.
samtools and Picard QC of the merged-replicate alignments; summarised in the MultiQC report.

deepTools plotFingerprint and plotProfile QC (enrichment and TSS profiles): plotted in the MultiQC report, not a sample result. FingerprintJSD is read from the qcmetrics file (sample_files) onto the D.SEQ.
ataqv's per-sample ATAC-seq QC JSON and its HTML viewer: QC. TSSEnrichment is read from the JSON (sample_files) onto the D.SEQ.
MACS2's peak table and gapped peaks: the same calls as the narrowPeak or broadPeak file the peaks rules register.
MACS2 summits (narrow mode): one point per registered peak, derived from the same call.

HOMER peak-to-gene annotation of the registered peaks (and of the consensus set): an annotation a user can rebuild from the registered files, and a peak row's one secondary slot is kept for its own losing variant (G-4).
MACS2 and HOMER QC plots and the FRiP, peak-count and annotation MultiQC custom-content files: QC, read from MultiQC's copies of the FRiP and peak-count files (module_tables).
The consensus peak set again as SAF and as presence/absence spreadsheets, and its UpSetR intersection files: reformats of the consensus BED the consensus rule registers.
atacseq's DESeq2 step is QC only: PCA, sample distances and the vst DESeqDataSet over the consensus counts, with no contrast. No differential result exists to register.
The same QC-only DESeq2 step over the merged-replicate consensus counts: PCA and sample distances, with no contrast.
IGV session file and its file list: points at the registered files, holds no data of its own.
Reference FASTA, blacklist, gene BED and aligner indexes (with --save_reference): reference files, not sample data.
